{{divhide|end}} }} This page documents [[tornado|notable tornadoes]] and [[tornado outbreak]]s worldwide in 2025. Strong and destructive tornadoes form most frequently in the [[United States]], [[China]], the [[Pampas]], the [[European Plain]], [[South Africa]], and [[Bengal]], but they can occur almost anywhere under the right conditions. Tornadoes also develop occasionally in southern [[Canada]] during the [[Northern Hemisphere]]'s summer and somewhat regularly at other times of the year across [[Europe]], [[Asia]], and [[Australia]]. Tornadic events are often accompanied by other forms of [[severe weather]], including strong [[thunderstorm]]s, winds, and [[hail]]. Worldwide, at least 104 tornado-related deaths have been confirmed: 67 in the [[United States]], 12 in [[Vietnam]], seven in [[Brazil]], four each in [[China]], [[Spain]], and [[Uganda]], two in the [[Philippines]], and one each in [[France]], [[Japan]], [[Portugal]], and [[Turkey]]. In the United States, the first two months of the year started off slightly below average, with generally scattered tornado activity. However, a major increase in activity began in March as the synoptic pattern became much more favorable for tornado outbreaks, [[Tornado outbreak of March 14–16, 2025|including the largest tornado outbreak on record for the month, which occurred mid-month.]] Significant and damaging outbreaks continued in the months of April and May, while June featured [[2025 Enderlin tornado|the first EF5 tornado]] in the United States since the [[2013 Moore tornado]], which occurred near [[Enderlin, North Dakota]] on June 20. In contrast to 2024, however, 2025 had a significantly inactive late season, with 172 tornadoes occurring from August through December, compared to 1,106 from March to June. This was due to multiple Arctic blasts bringing very cold, unsuitable air, and the fact that no hurricanes made landfall in the United States during the [[2025 Atlantic hurricane season|hurricane season]]. 2025 also had the highest number of violent tornadoes in a year since [[Tornadoes of 2013|2013]], with eight tornadoes worldwide receiving a rating of (E)F4 or higher. They are counted as their closest [[Enhanced Fujita scale|EF-scale]] equivalent on this table.{{clear}} ==January== === January 3–7 (United States)=== {{main|January 5–6, 2025 United States blizzard}} {{Tornado chart small|FU = 1|F0 = 2|F1 = 9|F2 = 2|F3 = 0|F4 = 0|F5 = 0|Enhanced=yes}} [[File:First US tornado in 2025.webm|thumb|The [[Tehama County, California]] EFU tornado on January 3, 2025.]] From January 3 to January 7, a [[January 5-6, 2025 United States blizzard|major winter storm]] passed over the [[contiguous United States]]. The storm system reached the [[West Coast of the United States]],{{Cite web |date=7 January 2025 |title=Early January Winter Storm Summary |url=https://www.wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/storm_summaries/event_reviews/2025/20250104.pdf|access-date=22 February 2026 |website=wpc.noaa.gov}} where it produced the first tornado of the year, a brief EFU tornado in rural [[Tehama County, California]], which caused no damage.{{cite news| last1=Parker| first1=Jordan| last2= Edwards| first2=Anthony| date=3 January 2025| title=Tornado spotted in Northern California, officials warn public to take shelter| url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/california/article/tornado-spotted-northern-california-20014277.php| url-status=live| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250104032514/https://www.sfchronicle.com/california/article/tornado-spotted-northern-california-20014277.php| archive-date=4 January 2025| access-date=4 January 2025| work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]]}}{{cite web |title=January 3rd, 2025 Tornado Event |url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSSTO&e=202501041627 |website=Iowa Environmental Mesonet |publisher=[[National Weather Service]] |access-date=4 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250104185524/https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSSTO&e=202501041627 |archive-date=4 January 2025 |location=Sacramento, California |date=4 January 2025 |url-status=live}} On January 4, a [[low pressure system]] organized over the [[Texas Panhandle]] and [[Oklahoma]]. Interacting with the existing cold air, the system’s [[warm front]] was predicted to generate severe thunderstorms across [[Southern United States]] on January 5, prompting the [[Storm Prediction Center]] to issue an enhanced risk for the region. The outlook included a 10% risk area for tornadoes, along with the potential for large hail and damaging winds.{{Cite web |date=5 January 2025 |title=Jan 5, 2025 0600 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook |url=https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/archive/2025/day1otlk_20250105_1200.html |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=spc.noaa.gov |language=EN-US}}{{Cite web |date=4 January 2025 |title=Jan 4, 2025 0600 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook |url=https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/archive/2025/day1otlk_20250104_1200.html |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=spc.noaa.gov |language=EN-US}} [[File:Damage Points SDE image-20250106-180223.jpg|thumb|left|High-end EF2 damage to a well-constructed shop building east of [[Marion, Louisiana]]]] On January 5, a small [[tornado outbreak]] occurred as a [[squall line]] of severe thunderstorms passed through the region, producing multiple tornadoes in [[Louisiana]], [[Arkansas]], [[Mississippi]], and [[Alabama]], including two strong tornadoes. A high-end EF2 tornado touched down near [[Marion, Louisiana]]. It completely destroyed a mobile home and a well-built shop building, damaged the roofs of multiple houses, and snapped numerous large trees. In Mississippi, a low-end EF2 tornado snapped or uprooted numerous trees and downed power poles as it passed to the north of [[Brooksville, Mississippi|Brooksville]]. High-end EF1 tornadoes caused moderate tree and structure damage in the rural Mississippi communities of [[Boon, Mississippi|Boon]] and [[Gwinville, Mississippi|Gwinville]]. A PDS tornado warning was issued for an EF1 tornado near [[Pelahatchie, Mississippi|Pelahatchie]],{{Cite web |last=Omega |first=Radar |date=January 5, 2025 |title=PDS Tornado Warning continues for Morton MS, Pelahatchie MS and Forkville MS until 8:15 PM CST |url=https://x.com/RadarOmega/status/1876078126192836714 |access-date=July 23, 2025}} damaged chicken houses, downed trees and power lines, and caused an indirect injury when a train ran into a downed tree that had fallen onto railroad tracks.{{cite news|url=https://www.wlbt.com/2025/01/06/train-crashes-into-tree-rankin-county/|title=Train crashes into tree in Rankin County|publisher=[[WLBT|WLBT-3]]|author-last=Ballou|author-first=Howard|date=5 January 2025}} A total of 14 tornadoes were confirmed, resulting in one indirect injury and no fatalities.{{cite web |author1=Various [[National Weather Service]] offices |title=Damage Assessment Toolkit |url=https://apps.dat.noaa.gov/stormdamage/damageviewer/ |website=DAT |publisher=[[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] |year=2025 |format=Interactive map and database}} {{clear}} === January 6 (Saudi Arabia) === As a red alert for severe weather was issued by the National Centre of Meteorology over the region around [[Mecca]] on January 6, a tornado was reported to have struck [[Rabigh]], which was reported by ''[[Gulf News]]'' to be the strongest ever recorded in the coastal region of [[Saudi Arabia]]. The National Centre of Meteorology also discussed plans to further research the tornado.{{cite web |url=https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/saudi/watch-video-powerful-tornado-hits-rabigh-in-saudi-arabia-safety-warnings-issued-1.500011383 |title=Watch video: Powerful tornado hits Rabigh in Saudi Arabia, safety warnings issued |author=Khitam Al Amir |date=6 January 2025 |access-date=8 February 2025 |work=[[Gulf News]] }} {{clear}} ===January 17 (Italy) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 0 | IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 1 |IF1 = 1 | IF1.5 = 1 | IF2 = 2 | IF2.5 = 0 | IF3 = 0 | IF4 = 0 | IF5 = 0}} [[2024–25 European windstorm season#Storm Gabri|Storm Gabri]] struck [[Italy]] on January 17, causing torrential rainfall, thunderstorms, strong winds, and multiple tornadoes, all of which occurred on the island of [[Sicily]]. An IF2 tornado impacted areas near [[Catania]], causing significant roof and tree damage, bending a metal truss electrical transmission tower in half, and rolling a [[living van|roulotte trailer]] {{convert|30|m|yd|abbr=on}}. Metal light poles were also bent, a semi-trailer was overturned, and sheet metal from buildings was scattered {{convert|500|m|yd|abbr=on}} up a hillside. An IF1.5 tornado struck the northern suburbs of Catania and blew a camper over, downed several trees and damaged the roofs of multiple buildings. A strong, long-tracked [[Multiple-vortex tornado|multiple-vortex]] IF2 tornado that struck areas outside of [[Avola]] downed numerous trees and power lines, toppled another electrical transmission tower, destroyed a masonry outbuilding, unroofed a house, and damaged the roofs of other homes.{{cite web |author1=Staff of the [[European Severe Storms Laboratory]] |title=European Severe Weather Database |url=https://eswd.eu/ |website=ESWD |publisher=[[European Severe Storms Laboratory]] |format=[[Map|Interactive map]] and [[database]] |year=2025 |access-date=2025-01-17 |archive-date=2022-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220920172917/https://eswd.eu/ |url-status=live }} In [[Augusta, Sicily|Augusta]], an IF0.5 tornado overturned a small [[Piaggio Ape|ape car]], damaged concrete monuments and decorations at a cemetery, downed trees and power lines, and tore sheet metal roofing from buildings. An IF1 tornado struck the outskirts of [[Licata]] as well, damaging crops and destroying greenhouses. A total of five tornadoes were confirmed.{{cite news|url=https://www.ilmattino.it/schede/scuole_chiuse_campania_allerta_meteo_domani_17_gennaio_sicilia_calabria_ultime_notizie-8597613.html|language=italian|title=Allerta meteo, le scuole chiuse domani in Campania: allarme anche in Calabria e Sicilia. L'elenco|work=[[Il Mattino]]}}{{Cite news|title=Severe Weather Forces School Closures in Sicily|url=https://cde.news/severe-weather-forces-school-closures-in-sicily/|publisher=CDE News}} {{clear}} === January 21 (Portugal) === [[2024–25 European windstorm season#Storm Garoe|Storm Garoé]] made landfall in [[Spain]] and [[Portugal]] on January 21, bringing strong winds, torrential rain, and severe weather in coastal areas.{{Cite news|url=https://euroweeklynews.com/2025/01/21/storm-garoe-strikes-spain-again-tornadoes-torrential-rain-and-flooding-fears-as-country-braces-for-more-chaos/|title=Storm Garoé strikes Spain again: Tornadoes, torrential rain, and flooding fears as country braces for more chaos|date=21 January 2025|author-last=Menendez-Roche|author-first=Marc}} During the late evening, an IF2 tornado tracked through rural areas near the community of [[Montevil]] in [[Setúbal District|Setúbal District, Portugal]]. Many large trees were snapped or uprooted along the path, and some were defoliated and stripped of their branches. Some crop damage also occurred, and power lines were downed. {{clear}} === January 23 (United Kingdom) === {{main|Storm Éowyn}} On January 23, Storm Éowyn made landfall in [[United Kingdom]], resulting in strong winds and heavy rain. An IF2 tornado moved through [[Holywell, Cornwall|Holywell]] and [[Quintrell Downs]], causing severe damage at the Trevornick Caravan Park, snapping many trees, and causing roof damage to homes. 46|work=NWS Storm Prediction Center|date=15 March 2025}} as a tornado outbreak featuring "significant tornadoes, some of which should be long-track and potentially violent," was expected throughout Another deadly EF3 tornado also tracked just east of the path of the long-track EF4 tornado, touching down while the latter was still on the ground. Tornadoes continued in Mississippi and Alabama throughout the afternoon and evening, including an EF2 tornado that struck [[Winterboro, Alabama]], damaging a high school and killing one person, and an EF3 that killed two people near [[Plantersville, Alabama]].{{cite report |url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSBMX&e=202503271927|title=NWS Damage Survey for 03/15/2025 Tornado Outbreak Update #13|author=National Weather Service in Birmimgham, Alabama|date=March 27, 2025|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|access-date=March 27, 2025}} Overall, seven people were killed in Mississippi and three more were killed in Alabama from tornadoes on the 15th.{{cite news|title=Mississippi tornado kills seven people, leaves several injured statewide|url=https://www.wdsu.com/article/mississippi-tornado-deaths-tylertown/64195949|date=18 March 2025|author=Erin Lowrey|publisher=WDSU}}{{cite news|url=https://www.wvtm13.com/article/alabama-tornado-outbreak-dead/64197920|title=Winterboro man whose home damaged for fifth time among 3 Alabama tornado deaths|publisher=WVTM|date=18 March 2025|author=Taylor Lang}} On March 16, a slight risk for tornadoes was issued for the [[South Atlantic States]]{{cite report|url=https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/archive/2025/day1otlk_20250316_1200.html|title=Mar 16, 2025 0600 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook|work=NWS Storm Prediction Center|author1=Darrow|author2=Moore}} as several weak tornadoes touched down across the [[East Coast of the United States|East Coast]]. In all, 118 tornadoes were confirmed in the outbreak, making this the largest tornado outbreak ever recorded in March. In addition, 42 people were killed from this outbreak,{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/42-dead-severe-storms-tornadoes-swept-us-rcna196672|title=42 dead in severe storms and tornadoes that swept across U.S.|publisher=NBC News|author1=Marlene Lenthang|author2=Kathryn Prociv|date=17 March 2025|access-date=7 April 2025}} including 23 tornadic deaths: Ten in Missouri, seven in Mississippi, and three each in Arkansas and Alabama. {{clear}} === March 15 (Uganda) === A powerful [[waterspout]] made landfall in [[Kalangala]], damaging or destroying hundreds of structures across at least five villages, including a police station, homes, and businesses. The strongest to impact the city, an EF1 tornado, injured one person after a roof collapsed on him.{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Chicago, Illinois|title=NWS Damage Survey for 3/19/2025 Tornado Event|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSLOT&e=202503210248&bbb=CCA|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=March 20, 2025|access-date=March 20, 2025}} {{clear}} === March 30–31 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|FU = 0|F0 = 21|F1 = 20|F2 = 3|F3 = 0|F4 = 0|F5 = 0|Enhanced=yes}} A widespread severe weather outbreak impacted the [[Midwestern United States|Midwestern]] and [[Southern United States]].{{cite report|url=https://www.spc.noaa.gov/products/outlook/archive/2025/day1otlk_20250330_1200.html|title=Mar 30, 2025 0600 UTC Day 1 Convective Outlook|work=National Weather Service|date=30 March 2025|access-date=1 April 2025|author=Kerr/Weinman}} 44 tornadoes touched down, including three EF2 tornadoes that occurred in the early morning hours of March 31, along with widespread damaging winds and large hail.{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Nashville, Tennessee|title=NWS Damage Survey for 3/30/2025 Tornado Event - Update #3|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSOHX&e=202504011542&bbb=CCA|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 1, 2025|access-date=April 1, 2025}}{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Jackson, Mississippi|title=NWS Damage Survey for 3/31/2025 Tornado Event|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSJAN&e=202503312147&bbb=CCA|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=March 31, 2025|access-date=April 1, 2025}}{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Lake Charles, Louisiana|title=NWS Damage Survey for 3/31/25 Grand Prairie Tornado Event|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSLCH&e=202503311653&bbb=CCA|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=March 31, 2025|access-date=April 1, 2025}} An EF1 tornado struck the downtown area of [[Dothan, Alabama]] on March 30, injuring five students when it hit [[Dothan Preparatory Academy]].{{cite news|url=https://www.wdhn.com/news/dothan-students-possibly-injured-after-suspect-tornado-hits-school/|title= UPDATE: Dothan students injured after suspected tornado hits school|author1=Richard Everett|author2=Aaron Dixon|publisher=WDHN}}{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Tallahassee, Florida|title=NWS Damage Survey for 03/31/2025 Tornado Event Update #1|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSTAE&e=202504012157|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 1, 2025|access-date=April 1, 2025}} The severe storms also resulted in two deaths and over 100,000 power outages.{{cite web | title=Daily Weather Update from FOX Weather: 2 dead as widespread severe storm threat continues Monday for 20 states | date=March 31, 2025 | url=https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/daily-weather-update-march-31-2025 }} The severe weather outbreak caused $2 billion in damage.{{Cite web |title=Events - U.S. Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters {{!}} Climate Central |url=https://www.climatecentral.org/climate-services/billion-dollar-disasters/events?s=endDate:desc&f=beginDate:between:19800101..20261231&ps=50 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=www.climatecentral.org |language=en}} {{clear}} ==April== === April 1–2 (Greece and Turkey) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 0| IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 0 |IF1 = 3| IF1.5 = 3| IF2 = 1| IF2.5 = 0| IF3 = 0| IF4 = 0| IF5 = 0}} Strong storms hit [[Southern Europe]], bringing severe weather particularly to [[Turkey]] and [[Greece]], spawning a small tornado outbreak.{{cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/greece-islands-rain-storms-crete-9bc2c21ecfc0a74255d937f9030a24a7|title=Severe storms batter Greek islands for a second day, with Crete hardest hit|work=AP News|date=1 April 2025}} On April 1, an IF1 tornado went through downtown [[Rhodes (city)|Rhodes]]. The next day, several tornadoes touched down in Turkey, including an IF2 tornado that tore through {{ill|Bostanlı, Andırın|tr|Bostanlı, Andırın|lt=Bostanlı}}, doing damage to a cinder-block building, ripping sheet metal off of other buildings, and deroofing one building. {{clear}} ===April 2–7 (United States)=== {{Tornado chart small|FU = 1|F0 = 35|F1 = 82|F2 = 33|F3 = 6|F4 = 0|F5 = 0|Enhanced=yes}} {{main|Tornado outbreak and floods of April 2–7, 2025|List of tornadoes in the outbreak and floods of April 2–7, 2025}} [[File:April 2–8, 2025 Radar Animation.webm|thumb|Radar animation of the tornado outbreak and floods.]] A slow-moving weather system resulted in both a devastating tornado outbreak as well as historic life-threatening flash floods throughout the [[Southern United States|Southern]] and [[Midwestern United States]] from April 2–7, spawning 157 tornadoes in total. The [[Storm Prediction Center]] (SPC) issued a [[List of Storm Prediction Center high risk days|high risk]] for the first day of the outbreak, April 2, which would be the busiest day as 74 tornadoes touched down across nine states. That evening, a high-end EF3 tornado destroyed multiple homes near [[Latty, Missouri]]. Later, a large, [[Multiple-vortex tornado|multiple-vortex]] high-end EF3 tornado impacted [[Bay, Arkansas|Bay]], [[Lake City, Arkansas|Lake City]], and [[Monette, Arkansas]], derailing two freight trains, and destroying high-tension power line trusses and several homes. A [[tornado emergency]] was declared for Lake City as the tornado struck,{{cite web |last1=Cann |first1=Christopher |title=Powerful storm roars into central US, threatens 'generational' rainfall |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2025/04/02/severe-storm-forecast-outlook-tornadoes-flooding/82771402007/ |website=USA Today}}{{cite news |title=Roofs Ripped Off, Semis Blown Over As Severe Weather Rips Across Midwest, South |url=https://weather.com/news/weather/news/2025-04-02-severe-tornado-live-updates-missouri-oklahoma-kansas-tennessee |access-date=3 April 2025 |publisher=The Weather Channel}} and injured eight people.{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Memphis, Tennessee|title=NWS Damage Survey for the April 2-5 Tornado Event - Update #6|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSMEG&e=202504161439|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 16, 2025|access-date=April 16, 2025}} Additionally, one indirect fatality occurred in association with an EF2 tornado that passed through [[Delta, Missouri]] as it moved along [[Missouri Route 25|Route 25]]; this tornado damaged approximately 200 structures along its path.{{cite web |title=Summary of the Severe Weather Outbreak of April 2, 2025 |url=https://www.weather.gov/pah/2025April2Severe |website=weather.gov |publisher=National Weather Service Paducah KY |access-date=6 April 2025 |language=EN-US}}{{cite news |date=2025-04-02 |title=Fire chief dies between Advance and Delta, Mo. after storms |url=https://www.kfvs12.com/2025/04/03/1-confirmed-dead-between-advance-delta-mo-after-storms/ |access-date=2025-06-08 |publisher=[[KFVS-TV|KFVS]]}} Tornado continued throughout the overnight hours into April 3. Another EF3 tornado damaged or destroyed buildings on the east side of [[Jeffersontown, Kentucky]] while an EF2 tornado injured three people along the [[Mississippi]]-[[Tennessee]] state line northwest of [[Walnut, Mississippi]]. A destructive high-end EF3 tornado devastated [[Selmer, Tennessee]], heavily damaging or destroying homes and businesses, obliterating manufactured homes, and killing five people. Soon after, a second tornado emergency was issued as another large, long-track high-end EF3 tornado passed near [[Slayden, Mississippi]] before crossing the state line and striking [[Grand Junction, Tennessee]] at EF2 strength, heavily damaging or destroying several homes, businesses, and manufactured homes, and collapsing a metal truss tower along its path. Two people were killed and three others were injured in a mobile home that was obliterated as the tornado crossed the state line.{{cite web |title=MEG Tornado Warning #85 |url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/vtec/event/2025-O-NEW-KMEG-TO-W-0085/radar/USCOMP-N0Q-202504030605/tab/info |access-date=3 April 2025 |website=Iowa Environment Mesonet |publisher=National Weather Service Memphis, TN |language=en}} Relatively lower, but still significant, tornadic activity continued over the next several days. On April 4, an EF2 tornado impacted the [[Lone Star, Texas]] area, heavily damaging homes, snapping trees, and tossing six vehicles.{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Shreveport, Louisiana|title=NWS Damage Survey for 04/04-05/2025 Tornado and Severe Thunderstorm Event - Update #6|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSSHV&e=202504232039|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 23, 2025|access-date=April 24, 2025}} The next morning on April 5, another EF2 tornado damaged or destroyed outbuilding and manufactured homes and injured one person near [[Wynne, Arkansas]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Memphis, Tennessee|title=NWS Damage Survey for April 2-6 Tornado Event - Update #7|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSMEG&e=202504232032|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 23, 2025|access-date=April 24, 2025}} Later, a long-tracked EF2 tornado caused widespread damage to homes, outbuildings, power poles, and trees as it passed near [[Thaxton, Mississippi|Thaxton]], [[Hurricane, Mississippi|Hurricane]], and [[New Albany, Mississippi]]. On April 6, an EF2 tornado struck [[Stringer, Mississippi]] killing a person in a [[mobile home]] that was obliterated. Weak tornadoes were observed on April 7 as the outbreak came to an end. Overall, nine tornadic fatalities occurred as a result of this outbreak, with many more being killed by the devastating flooding that accompanied it.{{Cite news |date=April 3, 2025 |title=Severe weather live updates: 'Life-threatening, catastrophic' flash floods and tornadoes to hit Midwest and South |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/weather/floods/live-blog/severe-weather-live-updates-life-threatening-catastrophic-flash-floodi-rcna199446 |access-date=April 3, 2025 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |language=en}} {{clear}} ===April 4 (Spain)=== {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 0| IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 0 |IF1 = 2| IF1.5 = 0| IF2 = 1| IF2.5 = 0| IF3 = 0| IF4 = 0| IF5 = 0}} [[File:Coria del Río tornado damage.jpg|left|thumb|The {{lang|es|Cortijo El Sequero}} warehouse that collapsed, killing three workers inside.]] As [[2024-25 European windstorm season#Storm Nuria|Storm Nuria]] made landfall in Iberia, at least three tornadoes touched down in the province of [[Province of Huelva|Huelva]].{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/sevilla/provincia/dos-hermanas/ultimo-adios-dos-hermanas-hermanos-fallecidos-derrumbe-20250406120403-nts.html|title=Último adiós en Dos Hermanas a los hermanos fallecidos por el derrumbe de una nave en Coria del Río|author=Valme J. Caballero|date=6 April 2025|work=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=Spanish}} An IF1 tornado was confirmed in [[San Bartolomé de la Torre]], collapsing a greenhouse and injuring four workers. Another IF1 tornado struck [[Moguer]], damaging crops and trees. A strong IF2 tornado struck the town of [[Coria del Río]], collapsing an agricultural warehouse and killing three workers. {{clear}} === April 17–20 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|FU = 4|F0 = 22|F1 = 26|F2 = 4|F3 = 1|F4 = 0|F5 = 0|Enhanced=yes}} [[File:Omaha-Bennington EF3 Tornado.png|left|thumb|250x250px|EF3 tornado in [[Bennington, Nebraska]].]] A four-day outbreak of tornadoes took place from April 17–20 across the [[Midwestern United States|Midwest]] and parts of the [[Southern United States|South]] as a slow-moving upper-level trough moved through the region. On April 17, an intense tornado touched down northeast of [[Bennington, Nebraska]], producing low-end EF3 damage before later causing additional damage in [[Nashville, Nebraska|Nashville]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Omaha, Nebraska|title=NWS Damage Survey for 04/17/2025 Tornado Event|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSOAX&e=202504182157|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=April 18, 2025|access-date=April 18, 2025}} Additionally, a very large high-end EF1 tornado prompted the issuance of a [[tornado emergency]] for the city of [[Essex, Iowa]].{{Cite web |date=April 19, 2025 |title=NWS Damage Survey for 04/17/25 Tornado Event - Update #1 |url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSOAX&e=202504200058 |website=mesonet.agron.iastate.edu}} Tornado activity remained relatively low for the remainder of the outbreak, though a high-end EF1 tornado killed one and injured two as it destroyed homes in the town of [[Spaulding, Oklahoma]] on April 20. This was the only tornadic fatality of the outbreak.{{cite web |last1=Wallace |first1=Josh |title=Oklahoma tornado kills 1, destroys homes in Hughes County |date=April 20, 2025 |url=https://www.koco.com/article/oklahoma-tornado-kills-1-destroys-homes-hughes-county/64534132 |publisher=KOCO News 5 |access-date=22 April 2025}} However, two people were killed due to flooding related to the storm system in Oklahoma.{{cite news |title=Tornado-producing storm deals deadly flooding and large hail to Oklahoma and Texas |url=https://ny1.com/nyc/news/news/2025/04/20/police--2-dead-in-oklahoma-flooding-as-region-remains-under-severe-weather-watch |access-date=May 17, 2025 |publisher=NY1 |agency=Associated Press |date=April 20, 2025}} {{clear}} === April 27–30 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|FU = 12|F0 = 14|F1 = 16|F2 = 5|F3 = 1|F4 = 0|F5 = 0|Enhanced=yes}} [[File:An aircraft hangar completely swept away at Seymour Airport.jpg|left|thumb|An aircraft hangar completely swept away at low-end EF2 intensity in Seymour Airport.]] A tornado outbreak lasting four days took place across parts of the [[Midwestern United States|Midwest]], [[Southern United States]], and [[Great Plains]] regions of the US from April 27–30. On April 27, activity was focused on [[Nebraska]], with several tornadoes, including three rated EF2, being confirmed. The [[Bingham, Nebraska|Bingham]]-[[Ashby, Nebraska|Ashby]] tornado in particular was the widest ever confirmed by the National Weather Service in [[North Platte, Nebraska|North Platte]], at {{convert|2200|yd|m}}.{{cite web | title=IEM :: PNS from NWS LBF | website=Iowa Environmental Mesonet | date=2025-05-02 | url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSLBF&e=202505021708 | access-date=2025-07-22}} The following day, a moderate risk for severe weather was forecasted, driven by a 15% chance for significant tornadoes; this moderate risk was centered on the [[Upper Midwest]] region of the United States.{{cite web | last=Kirwan | first=Hope | title=Tornadoes, hail possible for much of Wisconsin on Monday evening | website=WPR | date=2025-04-28 | url=https://www.wpr.org/news/tornadoes-hail-possible-wisconsin-monday | access-date=2025-07-22}} Activity largely failed to materialize, with just 12 tornadoes being confirmed, seven of which occurred in [[Wisconsin]].{{cite web | title=Preliminary info on the April 28, 2025 Tornadoes | publisher=NOAA's National Weather Service | date=2025-05-27 | url=https://www.weather.gov/mpx/prelim28Apr2025_tornadoes | ref={{sfnref|NOAA's National Weather Service|2025}} | access-date=2025-07-22}} More severe weather occurred the following day, with tornadoes occurring in [[Oklahoma]], [[Arkansas]], [[Missouri]] and [[Texas]]. The strongest of these tornadoes was rated EF3 after tearing through parts of [[Seymour, Texas]], including the Seymour Airport.{{cite web | title=Storm Events Database | website=National Centers for Environmental Information | date=2025-04-29 | url=https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/stormevents/eventdetails.jsp?id=1254067 | ref={{sfnref|National Centers for Environmental Information|2025}} | access-date=2025-07-22}} The outbreak concluded the next day, with several more tornadoes being confirmed, including one rated EF2 after damaging multiple farms in [[Fayette County, Illinois]].{{cite web | title=IEM :: PNS from NWS LSX | website=Iowa Environmental Mesonet | date=2025-05-02 | url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSLSX&e=202505020052 | access-date=2025-07-22}} In all, 48 tornadoes were confirmed in this outbreak. {{clear}} ==May== === May 2–4 (Europe) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 3 | IF0 = 1 | IF0.5 = 0 |IF1 = 6 | IF1.5 = 4 | IF2 = 0| IF2.5 = 0| IF3 = 0| IF4 = 0| IF5 = 0}} A severe weather outbreak produced scattered tornadoes across [[Europe]] from May 2–4, producing a total of 14 tornadoes across several countries. On May 2, conditions in [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberia]], namely a [[cold front]] pulling warm, moist air from the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] into an unstable environment with high wind shear, allowed for the development of long-lasting [[supercell]]s.{{cite web |url=https://www.estofex.org/cgi-bin/polygon/showforecast.cgi?text=yes&fcstfile=2025050306_202505011945_2_stormforecast.xml |date=1 May 2025 |author=Tuschy |work=ESTOFEX |title=ESTOFEX Storm Forecast valid 02 May 06:00 – 03 May 06:00 UTC 2025}} Two tornadoes touched down in eastern [[Portugal]]: one IF1.5 tornado near [[Beja, Portugal|Beja]] caused significant roof damage{{cite web|date=5 June 2025|url=https://www.ipma.pt/pt/media/noticias/news.detail.jsp?y=2025&f=Tornado_alentejo_02052025.html|title=Tornados em 2 e 3 de maio - Atualização|language=pt|work=[[Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera|IPMA]]|trans-title=Tornadoes on May 2 and 3 - Update}} while another IF1 tornado near [[Campo Maior, Portugal|Campo Maior]] caused widespread damage to the neighborhood of Degolados and injured one person.{{cite news |url=https://cnnportugal.iol.pt/fenomeno-extremo/ventos-fortes/queda-de-arvores-e-destruicao-de-casas-tornado-tambem-causou-estragos-em-campo-maior/20250502/6814d0cbd34e3f0bae9da15e |title=Queda de árvores e destruição de casas. Tornado também causou estragos em Campo Maior |date=2 May 2025 |language=pt |trans-title=Trees fell and houses were destroyed. Tornado also caused damage in Campo Maior |author=Agência Lusa |work=CNN Portugal}} Remnants of this system continued to create a risk of severe weather in Portugal the next day,{{cite web |url=https://www.estofex.org/cgi-bin/polygon/showforecast.cgi?text=yes&fcstfile=2025050406_202505021842_2_stormforecast.xml |author=Tuschy |date=2 May 2025 |work=ESTOFEX |title=ESTOFEX Storm Forecast valid 03 May 06:00 – 04 May 06:00 UTC 2025}} as a waterspout moved ashore off the coast of [[Sesimbra]] and a large IF1 tornado tracked through [[Sardoal]] in central Portugal. Similar conditions in parts of [[Southern Europe]] spawned an IF1.5 tornado in [[Turkey]] on May 3 and a [[landspout]] tornado in [[Cyprus]] the next day. Throughout [[Central Europe]], conditions were similar to Iberia, supporting supercell development. Three tornadoes ravaged forests and damaged buildings throughout [[Germany]] on May 3, and the weakening system produced two tornadoes in [[Belarus]] the next day, concluding the outbreak. {{clear}} === May 4 (Guadeloupe) === On the afternoon of May 4, a rare tornado struck parts of [[Baie-Mahault]] on the [[French West Indies#French Caribbean|French Caribbean]] island of Guadeloupe, producing localized structural damage in the residential neighbourhood of Belcourt. Strong, concentrated winds uprooted trees, blew debris across streets, and damaged roofs and light structures in several homes. Trees were snapped or uprooted in the vicinity, and local emergency services responded to calls for assistance in the aftermath of the event.{{cite news |title=Tornado flips vehicle and injures farmhand near Frankland River |publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation |date=June 4, 2025 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-06-04/tornado-frankland-river-western-australia-storms/105373206 |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=WA storm tornado flips ute and damages farm machinery |work=The Watchers |date=June 4, 2025 |url=https://watchers.news/2025/06/04/tornado-tosses-vehicles-damages-farm-frankland-river-western-australia/ |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === June 4 (Germany) === A strong IF2 tornado occurred in [[Baden-Württemberg]] and [[Bavaria]] and struck the community of [[Donaustetten]]. Birch trees were snapped, multiple houses were damaged, and several vehicles, lampposts and other objects were damaged severely. {{clear}} === June 5 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|FU=11|F0=2|F1=2|F2=3|F3=0|F4=0|F5=0}} [[File:Mobile home swept away.jpg|right|thumb|286x286px|A mobile home swept away near [[Lubbock, Texas]].]] A single supercell produced a [[Tornado family|family]] of eight tornadoes as it moved eastward towards the [[Lubbock metropolitan area|Lubbock, Texas metropolitan area]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Lubbock, Texas|title=NWS Damage Survey for 06/05/2025 Tornado Event|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSLUB&e=202506111806|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=June 11, 2025|access-date=June 12, 2025}} The second tornado was a large, strong EF2 tornado that moved through open desert near the town of [[Morton, Texas|Morton]], flipping center pivots and snapping wooden power poles. The tornado was highly photographed and videoed by nearby [[storm chasing|storm chasers]], and it was researched by nearby research teams during the LIFT Project. Dr. [[Sean Waugh]], with the [[National Severe Storms Laboratory]] (NSSL), researched the tornado. Using the NSSL Hail Camera Truck, positioned {{convert|200|m|yd}} away from the tornado, he captured a {{convert|1.6|in|cm|adj=mid|-diameter}} hailstone that was "being ejected from the tornado" at speeds up to {{convert|202|mph|km/h|abbr=on}}. The hailstone was only visible to the camera for six frames; a total of 0.0182 seconds.{{cite web |last1=Waugh |first1=Sean |author1-link=Sean Waugh |title=Hail Camera captures hailstone moving between 120-202 mph! |url=https://www.linkedin.com/posts/sean-waugh-00204932a_hail-camera-captures-hailstone-moving-between-activity-7351728752701108224-wOIb/ |publisher=National Severe Storms Laboratory |access-date=18 July 2025 |location=National Weather Center |date=17 July 2025}} The supercell also produced two other EF2 tornadoes along with two EF1 tornadoes and three EFU tornadoes. One of the EF1 tornadoes injured two people in a trailer park northeast of [[Smyer, Texas|Smyer]]. A swath of very strong outflow winds up to {{convert|115|mph|kph|abbr=on}} and very large hail up to {{convert|2.5|in|cm|abbr=on}} in diameter impacted western and southwestern [[Lubbock, Texas|Lubbock]] following the dissipation of the final tornado. Windows and skylights were shattered, and trees and roofs were damaged throughout this area. Two other weak tornadoes also touched down earlier that day. {{clear}} === June 15 (Armenia) === On the afternoon of June 15, a damaging IF1.5 tornado struck the town of [[Aparan]] and the nearby village of [[Lusagyugh, Aragatsotn|Lusagyugh]], causing widespread structural and infrastructure damage. The tornado tore roofs from residential and public buildings and damaged large sections of the local power and transportation network. Damage assessments by regional authorities reported that the roofs of approximately 20 apartment buildings and 86 homes were damaged, along with three schools, a cultural center, several administrative and law enforcement buildings, and numerous government facilities. Around 70 power lines were downed, 30 vehicles were damaged, and more than 100 trees were snapped or uprooted. A total of five people were injured, primarily by flying debris and collapsing roofing materials. Emergency services and municipal crews were deployed to clear debris and restore utilities in the aftermath.{{cite news |title=Strong winds damage dozens of buildings in Aparan and nearby villages, several injured |work=Armenpress |date=June 15, 2025 |url=https://armenpress.am/eng/news/aparan-storm-damage-buildings-injured |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Tornado causes heavy damage to homes, schools and infrastructure in Aragatsotn Province |work=News.am |date=16 June 2025 |url=https://news.am/eng/news/aragatsotn-tornado-damage-aparan-lusagyugh |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === June 17 (Norway) === A strong IF2 tornado struck a campsite near [[Støren]] in [[Trøndelag]], Norway. Several caravans were tossed and flipped, some of which landed in the [[Gaula (Trøndelag)|Gaula]]. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted, a barn was damaged, light poles were downed and outdoor furniture was tossed around. No injuries or fatalities occurred. {{clear}} === June 17–18 (Russia) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 1 | IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 0 |IF1 = 4 | IF1.5 = 1 | IF2 = 3 | IF2.5 = 0 | IF3 = 0 | IF4 = 0 | IF5 = 0 }} [[File:Siberia tornado scar 17 Jun 2025.png|thumb|left|An F3/IF1.5 tornado left a large scar through the Siberian forest.]] At least 9 tornadoes touched down in unpopulated areas of Russia. On June 17, a long track F3/IF2 tornado tracked through [[Khanty-Mansia]].{{cite web |url=https://tornado.gispsu.ru/ |script-title=ru:Смерчи в лесной зоне России |work=[[Perm State University]] |format=[[Map|Interactive map]] and [[database]]}} It was found to be over {{convert|2.5|km|mi|abbr=on}} wide, tying it for the [[List of tornadoes by width|widest]] tornado ever recorded in Russia. The tornado was likely stronger than its rating, but the only damage it inflicted was to trees. The next day, an IF2 tornado snapped reinforced concrete power poles near [[Kirovskaya, Rostov Oblast|Kirovskaya]] in [[Rostov Oblast]]. {{clear}} === June 19–22 (United States and Canada) === {{Main|Tornado outbreak and derecho of June 19–22, 2025|List of tornadoes in the outbreak and derecho of June 19–22, 2025|2025 Enderlin tornado}} {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|FU=2|F0=10|F1=16|F2=5|F3=1|F4=0|F5=1}}{{multiple image | align = right | direction = vertical | header = | width = 190 | image1 = Spiritwood Tornado a mile NW of Urbana, ND.png | alt1 = | caption1 = A large EF3 tornado in Barnes County on June 20. | image2 = Enderlin, North Dakota EF5 tornado.jpg | caption2 = An EF5 tornado southeast of Enderlin, North Dakota. | alt2 = }} A period of enhanced severe weather occurred across both the northern part of the United States, and the southern part of Canada from June 19–22. [[Environment and Climate Change Canada|Environment Canada]] confirmed that 10 tornadoes touched down in [[Saskatchewan]], including two EF2 tornadoes on June 19.{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/saskatchewan/environment-canada-eight-possible-tornadoes-1.7566572 |title=Environment and Climate Change Canada investigating 8 possible tornadoes across Saskatchewan |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=20 June 2025 |access-date=21 June 2025 |last=Tram |first=Jeffrey}} On June 20, a significant and damaging outbreak unfolded over [[North Dakota]]. During the event, an intense EF3 tornado impacted a farmstead in western [[Barnes County, North Dakota|Barnes County]], near [[Spiritwood, North Dakota|Spiritwood]]. A large steel building and two-story residence were damaged or destroyed, while another farmhouse to the north was demolished. An EF2 tornado impacted areas south of [[Valley City, North Dakota|Valley City]], causing considerable roof damage to one home. A large and exceptionally violent EF5 tornado struck at nightfall as it passed east of [[Enderlin, North Dakota|Enderlin]], tossing train cars, devastating farmsteads, and killing three people.{{Cite web |title=At least 3 dead in North Dakota as severe weather sweeps across region |url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/3-dead-north-dakota-severe-weather-sweeps-region/story?id=123068015 |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=ABC News |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2025 |title=Public Information Statement |url=https://forecast.weather.gov/product.php?site=NWS&issuedby=FGF&product=PNS&format=CI&version=3&glossary=0 |access-date=June 23, 2025}} The tornado was initially rated as an EF3 after it happened,{{Cite web |date=June 21, 2025 |title=We have 3 teams surveying damage from last night's storms. Preliminary tornado ratings based on damage: West of Valley City: EF-3+ South of Valley City: EF-2+ Enderlin area: EF-3+ Bemidji area: no update These ratings are PRELIMINARY and subject to change. #mnwx #ndwx|url=https://x.com/NWSGrandForks/status/1936529003092890046?s=20|access-date=January 14, 2026 |website=[[Twitter]] |language=en}} however on October 6, a reanalysis conducted by National Weather Service surveyors, and forensic engineers confirmed wind speeds exceeded the threshold needed for the EF5 rating. The upgrade was prompted by the tornado derailing 33 train cars,{{cite web | title=Research assists with rating historic EF5 tornado in northern United States | date=October 6, 2025 | url=https://news.westernu.ca/2025/10/ef5-tornado-enderlin/ }} an event that was not initially used for damage assessment but became a key factor based on new research. This reclassification marks the first such rated tornado in the United States in 12 years, since the 2013 Moore, Oklahoma tornado.{{cite web | last=Gilbert | first=Mary | title=First EF5 tornado to strike the US in over a decade just confirmed by experts | publisher=CNN | date=2025-10-06 | url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/10/06/weather/ef5-tornado-north-dakota-climate | access-date=2025-10-07}} A powerful derecho also produced hurricane-force winds across [[Montana]], [[North Dakota]], [[Minnesota]], and [[South Dakota]], with the highest confirmed wind gust reaching {{convert|120|mph|kph|abbr=on}} near [[Bemidji, Minnesota]].{{cite web | title=IEM :: PNS from NWS FGF | website=Iowa Environmental Mesonet | date=2025-06-27 | url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSFGF&e=202506271801 | access-date=2025-06-30}} The remnants of the system, a line of thunderstorms, moved into [[New York (state)|New York]] by the early morning hours of June 22, spawning an EF1 tornado that struck [[Clark Mills, New York|Clark Mills]]. The tornado snapped and uprooted many trees, with several trees falling on homes, which resulted in three fatalities.{{Cite web | author=Kozlowski, M. J. | date=2025-06-23 | title=EF1 tornado confirmed in the town of Clark Mills | url=https://cnycentral.com/news/local/ef1-tornado-confirmed-in-the-town-of-clark-mills}} {{clear}} === June 22–23 (Brazil) === {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|FU=5|F0=0|F1=0|F2=1|F3=0|F4=0|F5=0}} At least six tornadoes were confirmed in [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]] from June 22–23. The strongest of these, rated EF2 by PREVOTS, damaged infrastructure in the [[Passos Maia]] municipality and also downed large trees.{{cite web | title=SC registra ao menos seis tornados durante transição do outono para inverno | website=NSC Total | date=2025-07-04 | url=https://www.nsctotal.com.br/noticias/sc-registra-ao-menos-seis-tornados-durante-transicao-do-outono-para-inverno | language=pt | ref={{sfnref|NSC Total|2025}} | access-date=2026-01-14}}{{Cite web | last = Schild, Touchtenhagen | first = Guilherme | author2 = Vitor Goede; Lais Santos | title = Trails of destruction caused by tornadoes and extreme winds in Santa Catarina between June 22 and 23, 2025 | date = July 2025 | url = https://prevots.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Relatorio_Tornados-em-Santa-Catarina.pdf | publisher = PREVOTS – Platform for Records and Voluntary Network of Severe Storm Observers | access-date = January 14, 2026 }} {{clear}} === June 28–29 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|FU=1|F0=2|F1=2|F2=2|F3=1|F4=0|F5=0}} [[File:Gary, SD Tornado.png|thumb|left|An EF3 tornado near Gary in Deuel County, South Dakota.|222x222px]] A small tornado event occurred late on June 28 and into the early morning of June 29 across [[South Dakota]] and southern [[Minnesota]]. A prolific supercell produced a few tornadoes across [[Deuel County, South Dakota]], before moving into [[Yellow Medicine County, Minnesota]] and dissipating. The first tornado of the storm, rated at mid-range EF2, touched down southwest of [[Altamont, South Dakota|Altamont]]. A silo and shed were destroyed, while a farmhouse was shifted off its foundation. [[File:Farmhouse South Dakota June 2025.jpg|thumb|A two-story farmhouse was swept off its foundation near [[Gary, South Dakota]].|235x235px]] After the EF2 tornado dissipated, the parent storm would begin its cycling process, and later produced a high-end EF3 tornado east of [[Clear Lake, South Dakota|Clear Lake]]. This tornado exhibited multiple vortex breakdowns, crossed [[South Dakota Highway 22|SD 22]] in a narrow “drill bit” formation, and impacted a farmstead at high-end EF3 intensity. A two-story residence was completely swept away, several vehicles and farming equipment were thrown and were majorly mangled, trees were debarked, and several outbuildings and silos were destroyed. Two people were injured before the tornado dissipated southwest of [[Gary, South Dakota|Gary]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Aberdeen, South Dakota|title=NWS Damage Survey for 06/28/2025 Tornado Event Update #2|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSABR&e=202507021938|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=July 2, 2025|access-date=July 2, 2025}} A large, and rainwrapped EF2 tornado struck a ranch and injured two people just after touch down in rural [[Jackson County, South Dakota]], south of [[Kadoka, South Dakota|Kadoka]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Rapid City, South Dakota|title=June 28, 2025 White River Valley, SD Tornado|url=https://www.weather.gov/unr/2025-06-28_29|date=June 28, 2025|access-date=January 16, 2026}} During the early morning hours of June 29, several [[QLCS]] tornadoes were reported in the suburbs of [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]]. {{clear}} ==July== ===July 2 (China)=== A tornado rated at least EF2 struck industrial areas of [[Cangzhou]], [[China]]. Multiple factories and other buildings were levelled and vehicles were thrown long distances. Two fatalities and multiple injuries were reported.{{Cite news | title=Tornado damages vehicles and warehouses in Cangzhou, China, reports indicate two fatalities - The Watchers | url=https://watchers.news/2025/07/02/tornado-damage-cangzhou-china-july-2025/ | access-date=2025-07-07 | work=The Watchers|author=Rishav Kothari|date=2 July 2025}}{{Cite tweet | number=1940415437193576647 | title=Major tornado in Cangzhou, Hebei Province this afternoon, house leveled, cars tossed, multiple injuries, also hearing one or two fatalities. | user=Ericwang1101}}{{Cite web |title=China Tornado Database |url=https://www.fs121.com/tfile/20260310/c12a1131-36c0-4f51-9895-be745b83dbb3.xlsx}} {{clear}} === July 3 (Finland) === An IF2-rated tornado formed in [[Parkano]], [[Finland]] during Storm Ulla. No casualties were reported.{{Cite web |date=2025-07-10 |title=Parkanon ison metsätuhon aiheuttikin harvinaisen voimakas trombi |url=https://www.maaseuduntulevaisuus.fi/metsa/f09fa969-dc99-4c90-8e5a-9fbd5d86d2fb |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=Maaseudun Tulevaisuus |language=fi}} {{clear}} === July 7 (Europe) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 2 | IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 0 | IF1 = 1 | IF1.5 = 1 | IF2 = 2 | IF2.5 = 0 | IF3 = 0 | IF4 = 0 | IF5 = 0 }} A scattered day of severe storms across [[Central Europe]] spawned a few tornadoes. A waterspout made landfall and caused no damage north of [[Trieste]] in [[Northeast Italy]]. A strong IF2 tornado struck the community of [[Marcellano]], just west of [[Bastardo, Giano dell'Umbria|Bastardo]] in [[Central Italy]], downing and debranching numerous olive trees. At least one of the olive trees was lofted a few meters from where it stood. Buildings had their roofs and canopies damaged, power lines were tilted, light objects were tossed varying distances and fields were scoured. An IF1.5 tornado impacted [[Cigliano]] in [[Piedmont]], [[Italy]], causing a partial wall collapse of an auto repair shop and damaged to the roofs of other buildings in town. In [[Germany]], an IF1 tornado moved through southern [[Berga, Saxony-Anhalt|Berga]], damaging several roofs and tossing debris, which injured one person. Finally, an IF2 tornado moved through forested areas near [[Beloveža]], [[Slovakia]], snapping or uprooting hundreds of trees. In all, six tornadoes occurred. {{clear}} === July 9 (Belarus) === A strong IF2 tornado moved through the small village of [[Varkhi]] in Northern Belarus, damaging 27 residential buildings and 2 businesses. The [[European route E95|E95]] highway was blocked by trees that were downed from the tornado. Another brief tornado was documented of [[Ushachy]] but no damage was noted. {{clear}} ===July 12 (Utah)=== {{Main|2025 La Sal fire tornado}} [[File:Deer Creek fire tornado at a distance, by Jason Kirks from the Bureau of Land Management, July 12th, 2025.webp|thumb|Image of the tornado as it was forming.]] In the afternoon hours of July 12, 2025, a rare and significant [[Fire whirl|fire tornado]] occurred in the [[La Sal Mountains|La Sal mountain range]] near the small town of [[La Sal, Utah|La Sal]] in the U.S. state of [[Utah]].{{Cite web |last=Sharifi|first=Taban|date=2025-07-19|title=EF-2 Firenado from the Deer Creek Fire in Utah|url=https://www.weathernationtv.com/news/ef-2-firenado-from-the-deer-creek-fire-in-utah|access-date=2026-04-08|website=WeatherNation}}{{Cite web |last=Sistek|first=Scott|date=2025-07-17|title=Utah 'firenado' with 122-mph winds leaves behind significant damage|url=https://www.foxweather.com/extreme-weather/utah-firenado-deer-creek-fire-la-sal|access-date=2026-04-08|website=FOX Weather|language=en-US}} The tornado formed as part of the [[Deer Creek Fire]], a fast moving and destructive wildfire that formed 2 days earlier.{{Cite web |title=Charges filed in Deer Creek Fire that burned nearly 18,000 acres, sparked firenado|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/2025/10/04/charges-filed-deer-creek-fire-near/|access-date=2026-04-08|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Cross|first=Greta|title=Watch: 'Firenado' caught on video in Utah during Deer Creek Fire|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2025/07/18/firenado-utah-deer-creek-fire-video/85274328007/|access-date=2026-04-08|website=USA Today|language=en-US}} The tornado was approximately on the ground for 12 minutes{{Cite web |title=Are you scared of fires or tornadoes? Buckle up, because Utah just combined them.|url=https://www.sltrib.com/news/2025/07/17/utah-firefighters-witnessed/|access-date=2026-04-08|website=The Salt Lake Tribune|language=en-US}} and was nearly stationary as it moved north east. Strong winds influenced the formation of the [[Fire whirl|fire tornado]] over the Deer Creek Fire. Strong wind gusts coming off the La Sal mountain range, flowing over the mountains like a river over rocks. The mountains disrupted the wind, creating a body of swirling air, spinning flames into the mostly stationary fire tornado.{{cite web |title=Fire-Induced Tornado at Deer Creek Wildfire - July 12, 2025|url=https://www.weather.gov/gjt/12July2025_FireInducedTornado|access-date=August 16, 2025|website=weather.gov|location=Grand Junction, Colorado}}{{cite web |last1=Mohr|first1=Kylie|date=August 29, 2025|title=How a Utah wildfire created its own tornado|url=https://www.hcn.org/articles/how-a-utah-wildfire-created-its-own-tornado/|access-date=October 28, 2025|website=hcn.org|publisher=[[High Country News]]}} Rugged terrain and limited road access complicated [[Wildfire suppression|fire suppression]] efforts.{{cite news |last1=McMurdo|first1=Doug|date=July 17, 2025|title=Deer Creek Fire burns 15,655 acres, still at 7% containment|url=https://www.moabtimes.com/articles/deer-creek-fire-burns-15655-acres-still-at-7-containment/|access-date=October 28, 2025|work=[[The Times-Independent]]}} Due to damage found at a single family home, the tornado was rated EF2 on the [[Enhanced Fujita scale]]. {{clear}} === July 15 (Austria) === An IF2 tornado struck [[Taufkirchen an der Pram]] in Northwestern Austria, tearing [[photovoltaic panels]] off of roofs of buildings and tossing them considerable distances. Roof tiles, tree branches and other light objects were also tossed around. A shipping container was tossed onto a car as well. No injuries or fatalities occurred. {{clear}} === July 23 (Australia) === On the evening of July 23, a rare tornado struck the coastal suburb of [[City Beach, Western Australia|City Beach]] in [[Perth]], in the state of [[Western Australia]]. The tornado developed from a severe thunderstorm that rapidly intensified as it moved ashore, likely originating as a waterspout over the [[Indian Ocean]] before making landfall. The rotating storm produced strong, concentrated winds that damaged homes and infrastructure across the western suburbs. Multiple residences in City Beach and surrounding areas experienced significant roof damage, with sections of roofing removed and trees uprooted or snapped by the intense winds. Residents reported debris strewn across roads and gardens, and emergency services responded to dozens of calls for assistance as power outages and fallen trees disrupted daily life. Local meteorologists and witnesses described the storm's sudden onset, noting that the rapid development of the convective cell provided little warning before the tornado struck. The [[Bureau of Meteorology]] confirmed that the severe cell responsible for the damage exhibited characteristics consistent with tornadic activity. No fatalities were reported, though several households were left uninhabitable and repairs continued in the days following the storm.{{cite news |title=Freak tornado damages homes and uproots trees in Perth's City Beach |publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation |date=July 24, 2025 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-07-24/perth-tornado-damages-city-beach-homes-trees/105566566 |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Tornado rips through Perth's City Beach, leaving multiple homes damaged |work=PerthNow |date=23 July 2025 |url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/wa/perth/perth-weather-tornado-rips-through-city-beach-leaving-familys-million-dollar-home-without-roof-c-19452179 |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === July 27–28 (United States) === {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|FU=1|F0=2|F1=2|F2=2|F3=0|F4=0|F5=0}} [[File:High-End EF2 damage to a home.jpg|thumb|left|246x246px|High-end EF2 damage to a home near [[Watertown, South Dakota]].]] Back-to-back days of tornado activity focused over [[South Dakota]]. On July 27, a strong tornado occurred west of [[Watertown, South Dakota|Watertown]]. The tornado inflicted significant damage to a farmstead where a garage was swept from its foundation, and the main residence had only interior walls left standing. Significant tree damage was also observed.{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Aberdeen, South Dakota|title=NWS Damage Survey for NWS Damage Survey for 07/27/2025 Tornado Event - Update #1|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSABR&e=202507301819|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=July 30, 2025|access-date=August 1, 2025}} The next day on July 28, an isolated supercell produced three separate tornadoes in [[Gregory County, South Dakota|Gregory County]]. The strongest of them was an EF2 tornado that broke wooden power poles and inflicted major damage to a single-family residence and two nearby outbuildings. The tornado lifted just before entering the city of [[Bonesteel, South Dakota|Bonesteel]].{{cite report|author=National Weather Service in Sioux Falls, South Dakota|title=NWS Damage Survey for 07/28/25 Tornado Event Update 1|url=https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/wx/afos/p.php?pil=PNSFSD&e=202507312141|publisher=Iowa Environmental Mesonet|date=July 31, 2025|access-date=August 1, 2025}} {{clear}} ==August== === August 3 (Russia) === On August 3, a damaging tornado struck a rural area of the [[Jewish Autonomous Oblast]] in [[Russian Far East|Russia's Far East]], producing localized but significant infrastructure damage. The tornado snapped and uprooted trees and caused structural impacts to utility infrastructure, including the bending and partial collapse of several high-voltage power transmission towers, resulting in temporary power disruptions to nearby communities. Light structural and agricultural damage was also reported along the tornado's path. Damage surveys and photographic evidence indicated wind intensities consistent with an IF2 rating, making it the strongest documented tornado to occur in the Jewish Autonomous Oblast. No fatalities were reported, though emergency crews were dispatched to repair damaged power lines and clear debris following the storm.{{cite news |title=Смерч повредил линии электропередачи в ЕАО, несколько опор ЛЭП деформированы |work=РИА Новости |language=ru |date=August 3, 2025 |url=https://ria.ru/20250803/smerch-eao-linii-elektroperedachi-2025.html |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=В Еврейской автономной области прошёл смерч, повреждены опоры ЛЭП и деревья |work=Интерфакс |language=ru |date=4 August 2025 |url=https://www.interfax.ru/russia/eaoblast-smerch-povrezhdeniya-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === August 25–26 (Typhoon Kajiki) === Two days of tornadic unrest began late in the evening on August 25, as [[Typhoon Kajiki (2025)|Typhoon Kajiki]] made landfall in Vietnam. A powerful tornado struck [[Kim Bảng, Ninh Bình|Kim Bảng district]] in [[Ninh Bình province|Ninh Bình]].{{Cite web |date=2025-08-26 |title=Lốc xoáy ở Ninh Bình làm 1 người chết, hơn 200 nhà dân thiệt hại |url=https://tuoitre.vn/loc-xoay-o-ninh-binh-lam-1-nguoi-chet-hon-200-nha-dan-thiet-hai-20250826061809449.htm |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=TUOI TRE ONLINE |language=vi}} The tornado, though lasting only a few minutes, caused extensive damage to more than 200 homes and businesses. One 88-year-old woman was killed after a wall collapsed onto her, and 14 others were hospitalized with injuries. The following day, four additional tornadoes were reported across northern Vietnam. In total, the two-day outbreak resulted in at least one fatality and 14 reported injuries.{{Cite web |date=2025-08-27 |title=Tornado rips roofs off industrial buildings in Vietnam's Bac Ninh, no fatalities reported |url=https://news.tuoitre.vn/tornado-rips-roofs-off-industrial-buildings-in-vietnams-bac-ninh-no-fatalities-reported-103250827111011107.htm |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Tuoi tre news }}{{Cite web |last=Hanh |first=Minh |date=2025-08-26 |title=Vòi rồng bất ngờ xuất hiện trên bầu trời Hà Nội |url=https://laodong.vn/ban-doc/voi-rong-bat-ngo-xuat-hien-tren-bau-troi-ha-noi-1564170.ldo |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=laodong.vn}} {{clear}} === August 28–29 (Europe) === {{Tornado chart small IF-scale| IFU = 4 | IF0 = 0 | IF0.5 = 2 |IF1 = 4 | IF1.5 = 3 | IF2 = 0 | IF2.5 = 0 | IF3 = 0 | IF4 = 0 | IF5 = 0 }} The remnants of [[Hurricane Erin (2025)|Hurricane Erin]] established a strong upper-level [[trough (meteorology)|trough]] over [[Western Europe]], which, along with high [[Atmospheric instability|instability]] and [[wind shear]], created a volatile environment for storm development. The primary risk of these severe storms were extreme wind and rainfall, although some tornadoes were also predicted,{{cite web |url=https://www.severe-weather.eu/weather-forecast/severe-weather-forecast-outlook-for-europe-august-28th-2025-mk/ |title=Severe Weather Forecast / Outlook for Europe – August 28th, 2025 |author=Marko Korosec |website=Severe Weather Europe |date=28 August 2025}} particularly across [[France]] and [[Northern Italy]].{{cite web |url=https://www.estofex.org/cgi-bin/polygon/showforecast.cgi?text=yes&fcstfile=2025082906_202508272133_3_stormforecast.xml |title=ESTOFEX Storm Forecast |author=Tomas Pucik |date=27 August 2025 |website=ESTOFEX}} August 28 primarily featured strong wind events, with up to IF2-strength winds affecting parts of Northern Italy, although one rain-wrapped tornado caused minor damage in [[Somaglia]]. The next day, on August 29, several tornadoes occurred across Europe. In France, multiple supercell thunderstorms produced several tornadoes across the southwest and central regions. The strongest tornadoes were rated IF1–IF1.5, including events near [[Bias, Lot-et-Garonne|Bias]], [[Saint-Rabier]], and [[Martel, Lot|Martel]], where dozens of homes and businesses sustained roof damage, mobile homes were overturned, trees were snapped or uprooted, and residents were temporarily displaced. Around 30 houses were damaged in Saint-Rabier alone, and at least one person was slightly injured. Additional weaker tornadoes affected areas near [[Bergerac, Dordogne|Bergerac]], [[Marçay, Indre-et-Loire|Marçay]], [[Boisseuil]]-[[Saint-Hilaire-Bonneval]], and [[La Chapelle-sur-Aveyron]], producing scattered roof and tree damage. The events were documented and surveyed by [[KERAUNOS]], which confirmed multiple tornadic tracks across the affected departments.{{cite web |title=Plusieurs tornades observées en France les 28–29 août 2025 – bilan des enquêtes |publisher=KERAUNOS |language=fr |url=https://www.keraunos.org/actualites/bilans/tornades-france-28-29-aout-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Des mini-tornades endommagent des dizaines d'habitations en Dordogne et Corrèze |work=France Bleu |language=fr |date=August 29, 2025 |url=https://www.francebleu.fr/infos/meteo/des-tornades-degats-habitations-dordogne-correze-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}} Two tornadoes occurred in [[Italy]] on the 29th and impacted [[Verderio Superiore]], where roof tiles were blown off homes and trees were uprooted, and [[Goito]], where trees and a power line were damaged.{{cite news |title=Maltempo in Lombardia e Veneto: trombe d'aria e tetti scoperchiati |work=ANSA |language=it |date=29 August 2025 |url=https://www.ansa.it/lombardia/notizie/2025/08/29/maltempo-trombe-daria-tetti-scoperchiati |access-date=February 1, 2026}} Farther east in [[Poland]], brief tornadoes were observed near [[Śrem]] and [[Gniezno]]. The stronger of the two, near Gniezno, reached IF1.5 intensity, overturning vehicles, damaging trees, and injuring at least one person when a tree fell onto a car.{{cite news |title=Trąba powietrzna w Wielkopolsce przewraca auta i łamie drzewa |work=TVN24 |language=pl |date=August 29, 2025 |url=https://tvn24.pl/poznan/traba-powietrzna-gniezno-szkody-drzewa-auta-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === August 30 (Colombia) === An F1 tornado struck the town of [[Soledad, Atlántico|Soledad]] in the [[Atlántico Department]] of northern Colombia, producing widespread structural damage across multiple neighborhoods. According to local authorities and municipal reports, the tornado uprooted trees, damaged roofs, and caused significant structural impacts to over 700 homes in at least ten districts, including [[Los Robles, Soledad|Los Robles]], [[Los Almendros]], [[Ciudadela Metropolitana]], and [[Altos del Metro]]. Emergency response teams, including the Office of Risk and Disaster Management and the fire department, were deployed to assist affected residents, and the mayor declared a state of public calamity to coordinate humanitarian aid and recovery efforts. Eleven people were treated for injuries at local hospitals, most of which were minor.{{cite news |title='Tornado tipo F1 causó daños en 10 barrios de Soledad: hay 11 heridos' |work=El Universal |date=August 31, 2025 |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.co/regional/atlantico/2025/08/31/tornado-tipo-f1-causo-danos-en-10-barrios-de-soledad-hay-11-heridos/ |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Tornado en Soledad dejó más de 700 viviendas afectadas y 11 lesionados |work=Caracol Radio |date=August 31, 2025 |url=https://caracol.com.co/2025/08/31/tornado-en-soledad-mas-de-700-viviendas-resultaron-con-danos/ |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} === August 30 (Vietnam) === Severe thunderstorms associated with a broader [[East Asian monsoon|monsoonal disturbance]] produced a large tornado in [[Ba Vì district]], impacting [[Vật Lại Commune]] and nearby rural communities west of [[Hanoi]]. Several outbuildings and farm structures collapsed, and debris was scattered across roads and fields. Local authorities reported that dozens of houses sustained damage and multiple families were temporarily displaced while emergency crews conducted damage assessments and assisted residents with cleanup and temporary shelter. No fatalities were reported.{{Cite web |last=Phong |first=Báo điện tử Tiền |date=2025-08-30 |title=Hà Nội: Tôn bay, cây đổ do giông lốc |url=https://tienphong.vn/ha-noi-ton-bay-cay-do-do-giong-loc-post1774265.tpo |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=Báo điện tử Tiền Phong |language=vi}}{{cite news |title=Tornado damages dozens of homes in Ba Vì District after severe storms |work=VnExpress International |date=August 31, 2025 |url=https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/tornado-damages-dozens-of-homes-in-ba-vi-district-after-storms-4765123.html |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Whirlwind tears roofs off houses in Hanoi's outskirts |work=Vietnam News |date=31 August 2025 |url=https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1654321/whirlwind-tears-roofs-off-houses-in-ha-noi-outskirts.html |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} ==September== ===September 2 (France)=== Severe thunderstorms moving across [[Brittany]] during the afternoon of September 2 produced two tornadoes, including a significant long-track tornado that caused injuries and structural damage across several rural communes. A short bit later, a strong, [[Multiple-vortex tornado|multi-vortex]] IF2 tornado struck near [[Guéhenno]], where a narrow but intense damage swath extended nearly {{convert|20|km|mi|abbr=on}} through wooded and residential areas. Approximately ten homes were damaged, trees were snapped or uprooted, and debris was thrown hundreds of meters. Several mobile homes were overturned or displaced, with two occupants reportedly thrown from their shelter into a nearby field. Four people sustained minor injuries.{{cite web |title=Enquête KERAUNOS – Tornades du 2 septembre 2025 en Bretagne (Landévant et Guéhenno) |publisher=KERAUNOS |language=fr |url=https://www.keraunos.org/actualites/faits-marquants/2025/tornades-bretagne-2-septembre-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}}{{cite news |title=Plusieurs tornades frappent le Morbihan, des maisons endommagées et des blessés légers |work=Ouest-France |language=fr |date=3 September 2025 |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/morbihan/tornades-morbihan-degats-blesses-legers-2025 |access-date=February 1, 2026}} {{clear}} ===September 5 (Japan)=== {{Tornado chart small|Enhanced=yes|F0=0|F1=4|F2=2|F3=1|F4=0|F5=0}} A rare and destructive JEF3 tornado, spawned from the outer bands of [[Tropical Storm Peipah (2025)|Tropical Storm Peipah]], struck the city of [[Makinohara]] and neighboring town of [[Yoshida, Shizuoka|Yoshida]], both located within [[Shizuoka Prefecture]].
